title: Question 8: Prohibit Retail Sale of Adult Recreational Use Marijuana

context.text: Placed on the ballot by initiative petition: the Information for Voters labels it a law proposed by initiative petition on which no vote was taken by the Senate or the House of Representatives before May 6, 2026. The Legislature's Special Joint Committee on Initiative Petitions issued the legislative reports reproduced in the same booklet.

question.text: Do you approve of a law summarized below, on which no vote was taken by the Senate or the House of Representatives before May 6, 2026? Prohibit Retail Sale of Adult Recreational Use Marijuana: The proposed law would change the type and amount of marijuana that may legally be possessed in Massachusetts by repealing the laws that legalize, regulate, and tax the retail sale of adult recreational use marijuana in Massachusetts. The proposed law would also permit persons 21 years of age and older to possess 1 ounce or less of marijuana including no more than 5 grams in the form of concentrate, and to gift or transfer to another person 21 years of age and older 1 ounce or less of marijuana including no more than 5 grams in the form of concentrate. The proposed law would also impose a civil penalty of $100 and forfeiture of the marijuana for the possession of marijuana between the weight of 1 and 2 ounces. For persons 21 years of age and younger, the proposed law would make the possession of 2 ounces or less of marijuana a civil infraction subject to a $100 fine, forfeiture of the marijuana, completion of a drug awareness program and community service, and notification to their parents or legal guardian of the offense and penalties. The proposed law would allow currently licensed adult recreational marijuana businesses to apply on an expedited basis to become a licensed medical marijuana dispensary and to sell their remaining inventory of adult recreational marijuana to medical marijuana dispensaries. The proposed law would retain the Cannabis Control Commission but modify its authority so it would regulate only the medical marijuana market. The proposed law states that, if any of its parts were declared invalid, the other parts would stay in effect. The proposed law would take effect on January 1, 2028.

summary.text: The measure would repeal the laws that legalize, regulate and tax retail sale of adult recreational marijuana, while allowing adults 21 and older to possess up to 1 ounce, imposing civil penalties for larger amounts, letting licensed recreational businesses apply to become medical dispensaries, and limiting the Cannabis Control Commission to the medical market. It would take effect January 1, 2028. Statement of fiscal consequences (Executive Office for Administration and Finance): By repealing the laws that legalize and tax the retail sale of adult recreational use marijuana, the proposed law would reduce the amount that state and municipal governments receive from the taxation of those sales. In fiscal year 2025, taxation of the retail sale of adult recreational use marijuana raised approximately $280 million in state revenue and $50 million in local revenue. The state budget, which is supported by tax revenue, funds local aid for schools and municipal budgets.

measure.yesMeans: A YES VOTE would prohibit the legalization, regulation, and taxation of the retail sale of adult recreational use marijuana, and change the penalties for possession of marijuana.
measure.noMeans: A NO VOTE would make no change to the law relative to marijuana.

argumentsFor.text: In the 150-word argument in favor signed by Dr. Jeffrey Morgan of the Coalition For a Healthy Massachusetts, as printed in the Information for Voters: "Question 8 would keep personal possession of marijuana legal, keep medical marijuana legal, and stop commercial marijuana stores"

In the 150-word argument in favor signed by Dr. Jeffrey Morgan of the Coalition For a Healthy Massachusetts, as printed in the Information for Voters: "Modern concentrates and edibles have been linked to mental health conditions like psychosis, severe anxiety, and schizophrenia, particularly in young adults"

argumentsAgainst.text: In the 150-word argument against signed by Ryan Dominguez of the Massachusetts Cannabis Coalition, as printed in the Information for Voters: "For ten years, Massachusetts has regulated marijuana, ensuring that products are tested for safety, packaged and labelled properly, and sold in licensed businesses to adults 21 and over."

In the 150-word argument against signed by Ryan Dominguez of the Massachusetts Cannabis Coalition, as printed in the Information for Voters: "Question 8 would shut down hundreds of small businesses, kill thousands of jobs, and eliminate billions of dollars in state tax revenue."

researchNotes: Ballot text, official yes/no statements and fiscal statements are taken from the Secretary of the Commonwealth's 2026 Information for Voters booklet (PDF text extracted and checked by script). Arguments are quoted from the signed 150-word pro/con statements, which the Commonwealth states reflect the authors' opinions and are not certified as accurate. Both a signed pro and a signed con argument are printed. The booklet's own summary is the Attorney General's; the Secretary's page and Ballotpedia could not be fetched (bot protection), so the ballot list was confirmed from the booklet itself, which covers nine questions.
